teaser.text: Colgate-Palmolive sells the everyday products that people brush, wash, clean with, and feed to their pets. Its business is simple to describe but not to follow: a dollar enters through retailers and other customers, then leaves through products, factories, selling effort and the cash timing of the cycle.

blocks.heading: Where could Colgate-Palmolive's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $82.20 in October 2027, a −10% return, and $84.47 in October 2029, a −3% return. The forecast assigns 30% probability to the bear case, 50% to base and 20% to bull. The next dated test is the October 30, 2026 results release: North American volume and market share will show whether demand is stabilizing. Productivity savings must support growth without weakening brand investment. Hill’s branded demand, fresh-food adoption, buyback pace and the next dividend decision will shape the remaining paths.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Colgate-Palmolive?

paragraphs.text: The base assumes gradual volume improvement, pricing near the middle of guidance and productivity savings partly offset by brand investment. Management expects organic sales growth of one to four percent and mid-single-digit Base Business EPS growth. The bear case reflects North American volume down 3.9% and the prior guidance miss, when actual organic growth was 1.4%. The bull case requires broader oral-care gains, stronger Hill’s demand and savings that outlast inflation.

paragraphs.text: Capital spending cannot be treated as wholly avoidable, and stock compensation is not economically free simply because it is non-cash. Deducting stock pay produces a stricter analytical measure of free cash flow.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Colgate-Palmolive today?

paragraphs.text: At $94.11 a share, the company’s shares are worth $75,021.93 million, while enterprise value is $81,425.93 million. Enterprise value estimates the cost of owning the operating business, including lenders’ claims. Like buying a house with a mortgage attached, the buyer receives the asset but also takes on its financing obligations. The $6,404 million gap is net debt, so future cash must serve lenders before shareholders.

The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, measures what investors pay for each dollar of profit. Colgate’s trailing P/E is 37.3x, compared with 23.0x for the next twelve months. The gap partly reflects the $794 million after-tax impairment of its skin-health business in 2025. The charge was non-cash, but it still revealed that earlier expectations for Filorga had been too optimistic, especially in China.

blocks.heading: How much does Colgate-Palmolive pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend path rises from $2.14 to $2.22. The bear holds at $2.12, while the bull reaches $2.32. The starting floor is the declared $0.53 quarterly rate, or $2.12 annualized. The base assumes one-cent quarterly increases because the company has paid uninterrupted dividends for 63 years and the forward payout is roughly 52%. Weak volume and competing cash needs justify a pause in the bear case.

blocks.heading: Does Colgate-Palmolive cover its dividend with cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash generated by operations after spending on plants and equipment. From 2021 through 2025, Colgate generated $14,838 million of it. Shareholder dividends and buybacks used $14,663 million, while minority owners received another $773 million.

In 2025, actual buybacks were $1,210 million, although the board authorized up to $5 billion. An authorization permits future purchases; it is not itself a payment. New shares sold brought in $101 million, while net debt ended 2025 at $6,593 million. Dividends delivered cash, but buybacks created value only if Colgate bought its shares at worthwhile prices. The next test is whether its spending keeps customers choosing those brands.

Management’s one-to-four-percent organic-sales guide remains the base anchor, but actual volume, margins and cash conversion will determine whether that anchor holds.

blocks.heading: What has Colgate-Palmolive guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Colgate maintained its net-sales growth forecast at 2.0%–6.0%. It kept its organic-sales forecast at 1.0%–4.0%. The worldwide oral-care market is forecast to grow 8.9% over the same period, so Colgate’s organic guide looks modest.

blocks.heading: Did Colgate-Palmolive keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The record is mixed. Management forecast organic sales growth of 3% to 5% for 2025. It delivered 1.4%. The previous year was stronger, with 7.4% organic growth and 11% growth in base-business earnings per share, so shareholders should recognize that success while retaining the original 2025 forecast as an accountability benchmark.

blocks.heading: How have Colgate-Palmolive's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 quarter showed improvement, but the recovery still had important qualifications. Revenue increased year on year, and organic growth included both volume and pricing. Currency and Prime100 lifted the reported headline, so reported growth overstated the underlying pace.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Colgate-Palmolive's next release?

paragraphs.text: On October 30, Colgate will report its third-quarter results. Watch North American volume and market share together: volume measures units sold, while market share measures Colgate’s portion of consumer purchases. Higher shipments could merely mean retailers are rebuilding inventory. Organic growth may also look better as the private-label exit becomes an easier comparison, without showing faster underlying demand.
